intent: Specify the public API of `slab::Slab<T>` instantiated at `T = u32`: `new`, `with_capacity`, `insert`, `vacant_key`, `vacant_entry` with `VacantEntry::key` and `VacantEntry::insert`, `try_remove`, `remove`, `get`, `get_mut`, `contains`, `len`, `is_empty` and `clear`. In Lean these are `slab.Slab.new Std.U32`, `slab.Slab.with_capacity Std.U32 c`, `slab.Slab.insert s x`, `slab.Slab.vacant_key s`, `slab.Slab.vacant_entry s`, `slab.VacantEntry.impl.key e`, `slab.VacantEntry.insert e x`, `slab.Slab.try_remove s k`, `slab.Slab.remove s k`, `slab.Slab.get s k`, `slab.Slab.get_mut s k`, `slab.Slab.contains s k`, `slab.Slab.impl.len s`, `slab.Slab.is_empty s`, `slab.Slab.clear s`. Mutable borrows are threaded functionally: `&mut self` methods return the new slab (paired with their result); `get_mut` and `vacant_entry` return the borrowed value together with a backward function that rebuilds the slab (resp. entry) from the final value of the borrow.

manual_mutants.note: appending a new slot does not advance the next vacant key: the following insert hits an occupied slot
freed slot is not pushed on the vacant list (leak): keys are never reused, the slab grows while it has holes
manual_mutants.before: ok (o1, { entries := v, len := i, next := key })
manual_mutants.after: ok (o1, { entries := v, len := i, next := self.next })

manual_mutants.note: contains reports vacant slots as present
clear does not reset the next vacant key: the first insert after clear panics
manual_mutants.after: ok { entries := v, len := 0#usize, next := self.next }
ok { entries := v, len := self.len, next := 0#usize }

manual_mutants.note: is_empty tests the next vacant key instead of the number of values
get_mut on a vacant key overwrites the vacant-list link (corrupts the free list)

sibling_mutants.note: different (valid) reuse order: a released slot is linked in second on the vacant list (below the current top) instead of on top; every hole is still reused before the slab grows, insert still returns vacant_key()

edits.with_text:
def Slab.try_remove
  {T : Type} (self : Slab T) (key : Std.Usize) :
  RustM ((core.option.Option T) × (Slab T))
  := do
  let s ← alloc.vec.Vec.Insts.CoreOpsDerefDerefSlice.deref self.entries
  let o ←
    core.slice.Slice.get (core.Usize.Insts.CoreSliceIndexSliceIndexSliceT
      (Entry T)) s key
  match o with
  | core.option.Option.None => ok (core.option.Option.None, self)
  | core.option.Option.Some e =>
    match e with
    | Entry.Vacant _ => ok (core.option.Option.None, self)
    | Entry.Occupied val =>
      let i ← self.len - 1#usize
      let n ← alloc.vec.Vec.len self.entries
      if self.next < n
      then
        let o2 ←
          core.slice.Slice.get (core.Usize.Insts.CoreSliceIndexSliceIndexSliceT
            (Entry T)) s self.next
        match o2 with
        | core.option.Option.Some (Entry.Vacant nn) =>
          let (_, back1) ←
            alloc.vec.Vec.Insts.CoreOpsIndexIndexMut.index_mut
              (core.Usize.Insts.CoreSliceIndexSliceIndexSliceT (Entry T))
              self.entries key
          let v1 := back1 (Entry.Vacant nn)
          let (_, back2) ←
            alloc.vec.Vec.Insts.CoreOpsIndexIndexMut.index_mut
              (core.Usize.Insts.CoreSliceIndexSliceIndexSliceT (Entry T))
              v1 self.next
          let v2 := back2 (Entry.Vacant key)
          ok (core.option.Option.Some val, { entries := v2, len := i, next := self.next })
        | _ => fail panic
      else
        let (_, back1) ←
          alloc.vec.Vec.Insts.CoreOpsIndexIndexMut.index_mut
            (core.Usize.Insts.CoreSliceIndexSliceIndexSliceT (Entry T))
            self.entries key
        let v1 := back1 (Entry.Vacant self.next)
        ok (core.option.Option.Some val, { entries := v1, len := i, next := key })

bug_variants.note: Removing an already-vacant key overwrote the slot with Vacant(next) (fixed upstream in 2016: 'bugfix/test for remove when called on empty slot'; the pre-fix code predates the current API and cannot be extracted, so the same faulty logic is re-applied to the current try_remove's vacant branch). The vacant list becomes cyclic/corrupted: later inserts return an occupied key or panic, and try_remove on an absent key is no longer a no-op.
